subject: Transportation Systems
title: Roman Arch Bridges
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Roman Arch Bridges.

hook.text: Romans built stone arch bridges so well that some still carry traffic 2,000 years later.

buildup.text: The semicircular arch distributes weight outward and downward, compressing each stone tighter.

discovery.text: The Pont du Gard in France carries an aqueduct 160 feet above a river—no mortar, just precision-cut stone.

twist.text: Roman engineers didn't understand the physics. They built by rules of thumb passed down through generations.

climax.text: Their intuition was so good that Roman arch bridges outlasted the empire that built them.

punchline.text: They didn't know the math. They knew the craft.

quiz.question: How does a Roman arch bridge handle weight?
options: Weight is distributed as compression through the stone arch
